title: The Linear Representation Hypothesis for Vision-Language-Action Models
models: oracle Chen-Fliess construction on a planar unicycle-like system
action_head: regression head (OpenVLA-OFT MLP head mapping last-layer action-token states to an 8-step chunk)
methods: control-theoretic formalization of probing and steering (action-conditioned probes via path signatures)
signature exponential-family / GLM policy model, information-geometric steering derivation
steering along the head-Jacobian-mapped probe direction vs probe-only, static, random and simulator-gradient directions
question: Can the linear representation hypothesis be extended to VLAs so that action-conditioned future physical quantities are linearly probeable and linearly steerable, and does a pretrained VLA show this structure?
key_findings: Theory: for control-affine systems under Chen-Fliess conditions, a shared representation exists from which any finite set of propagated quantities is linearly probeable via signature features of the candidate action (Theorem 4.2); under a signature-GLM policy, moving along the probe-derived direction monotonically changes the expected quantity (Theorem 5.3).

Oracle: steering raises the expected lateral position from 0.000 to 0.134 to 0.255 for alpha = 0, 4, 8, at KL cost 0, 0.27, 0.98 nats; slope matches the predicted variance to 1e-11; saturates at 0.688.

OpenVLA-OFT probing (one LIBERO-10 task, held-out episodes): static probes read current mug positions (R2 0.58-0.97), but action-conditioned bilinear probes predict how a chunk moves them much better (increment R2 0.90-0.98 vs additive 0.80-0.95); for mug heights, propagated R2 0.95 / 0.96 with the increment vs 0.64 / 0.62 static only (Table 1).
Steering along the head-Jacobian direction increases the target quantity monotonically at 138 of 140 held-out states and matches the simulator-gradient oracle (cosine 0.98-1.00) (Table 2).

The probe direction without the head recovers at most ~75% of the effect, and the static probe direction often moves the quantity the wrong way (e.g. -11.3 mm for -d(mug1, plate)); random directions ~0 (Table 2).

Effects are small: median Jpsi(8) - Jpsi(-8) of 9-13 mm. Closed loop over 6 re-plans (2.4 s), EE-to-white-mug distance is 20 / 11.8 / 9 cm for alpha = -16 / 0 / 16, but the policy keeps heading for its original subgoal.

benchmarks: LIBERO-10 (single task: two mugs on two plates)
evidence.scale: 788 states from 50 layouts; 32 candidate chunks executed at 404 states; 20 held-out states per QoI for steering (140 total); closed-loop demo from one held-out episode
evidence.statistics: partial: held-out-episode R2, medians, percentage monotone; no CIs or tests
evidence.baselines: static probe, additive probe, nonlinear readouts, probe direction without head, random directions, simulator-gradient oracle

causal_validation: Yes: activation steering along derived directions changes the propagated physical quantity monotonically, compared with random, static and oracle directions.
closed_loop: Mostly measured on single-chunk outcomes with simulator execution; one closed-loop demonstration over 6 re-plans shows a cumulative few-centimetre path bias without changing the task subgoal.
limitations_stated: Experiments are a proof of concept for existence and realizability; finding a representation naturally suited to both probing and steering remains open.
Quantitative steering guarantees under finite probing error are left for future work.
Exact-probe assumption is an idealized limit.
critique: The steering intervention is on the last-layer action-token states right before a small MLP head, and the direction is the gradient of the probe-predicted quantity through that head. This is close to gradient-based action editing; agreement with the simulator gradient is expected, and it says little about higher-layer concept representations.
One LIBERO-10 task and one model (OpenVLA-OFT with a deterministic regression head); the theory targets stochastic diffusion/flow policies, but these are not tested.

The useful empirical point: static probe directions often fail or reverse the effect, while action-conditioned directions work. This matches 2608.13474 (progress not steerable) and 2610.20840 (geometry-matched edits can land on beliefs).

The theory (Chen-Fliess existence plus exponential-family steering) is largely existential and assumes a GLM policy form real VLAs do not have, so it explains rather than predicts the OpenVLA-OFT results.
one_line: A control-theoretic version of the linear representation hypothesis says future physical quantities should be linear in the representation given the planned action, and on OpenVLA-OFT action-conditioned probes predict object motion well and steering through the action head nudges the robot by about a centimetre, while naive static probe directions fail.
